# PROCESS — what I did this iteration (explainability; REQUIRED)

Iteration 1/1 (only iteration of the run). Parent = seed, val 0.725 (29 solid / 11 failing of 40).
**`prompt.md` was EMPTY (0 bytes) in the seed** — the agent ran with no system message at all,
and 100% of its instruction surface was `task_template.md`. That is the single biggest
untouched lever in this run, so this iteration authors `prompt.md` from scratch and
restructures the template's interaction contract.

No prior iterations exist (`RUNMAP.md` and `LEDGER.md` are empty; `rejected.jsonl` /
`history.jsonl` are absent). So there is nothing to build on and nothing refuted to avoid —
the whole SAFE burden falls on reading the 29 passing traces, which I did.

## Environment faults: NONE found
Every one of the 40 traces executed python successfully and produced an output file. No
permission errors, no missing binaries, no gateway/timeout failures, no container faults.
`rollout.error` is `None` on all 40. Every failure is a capability failure. (One environment
FACT, established below and load-bearing for the edits: no formula evaluator exists in the
sandbox — zero of 40 traces contain `data_only=True`, `soffice`, `libreoffice`, `pycel`,
`formulas`, `xlwings`, or `subprocess`.)

## Two facts I established BEFORE editing, because they invalidate the obvious fix

1. **The grader RECALCULATES formulas.** Passing tasks 42198, 52807, 41589, 39515, 49801 each
   wrote an Excel formula string with openpyxl, never computed a value, and scored **1.0**.
   11842 wrote 96 formulas and 94/96 recalculated to the expected value. So the tempting rule
   "write literal values, not formulas" would be FALSE and UNBOUNDED — it would have flipped
   5+ passing tasks. I narrowed it instead to the exact subclass that genuinely cannot
   survive openpyxl: **array/CSE formulas** (`MEDIAN(IF(...))` etc.), which openpyxl writes
   as scalar formulas so the inner condition collapses to the range's first cell.
2. **Cell-Level grading checks only `answer_position`.** So the "collateral damage from
   `pandas.to_excel`" argument is fatal only for Sheet-Level (341-40: 955 wrong cells, ALL
   of them cells it was never asked to touch, while its 8 requested cells were correct;
   535-20: 257 wrong, column selection correct). I therefore justified Rule 1 on fidelity
   and kept an explicit escape clause, rather than banning `to_excel` — 11 PASSING tasks use
   `to_excel` and must not be disturbed.

## Ranked issue list (clusters by # failing tasks, biggest first)

| rank | cluster | tasks | shared root cause | tag | planned change class |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | **Vacuous verification** — the "verify" turn cannot fail | 11/11 (all) | Template said "re-open output_path and print the values you wrote". Agents obeyed literally and printed something that must agree: formula text from a non-`data_only` handle (33722, 49036, 42354, 11842, 53647), hand-typed constants (38985), or a read-back using the SAME wrong offset as the write (48924, 5835). Zero information; agents then stopped confidently at 3–6 turns while scoring 0. | STRUCTURE + KNOWLEDGE | Ordered staged procedure + falsifiable pre-finish checklist (template); "Python is your only oracle" (prompt) |
| 2 | **Full-sheet `to_excel` destroys untouched cells** | 341-40, 535-20 (+ contributes to 5835, 51359, 38985) | `read_excel` → mutate → `to_excel` converts text-stored numbers/dates, blanks→empty, headers→`Unnamed: N`, drops trailing cols. Both Sheet-Level failures had CORRECT requested edits and failed 100% on collateral damage. | CONTRACT/KNOWLEDGE | State the in-place openpyxl idiom as the default, with an escape clause for generate/re-shape (prompt Rule 1) + Sheet-Level before/after diff (template stage 3.4) |
| 3 | **Array-formula written as scalar formula** | 33722, (mechanism behind 53647's error text) | openpyxl has no `ArrayFormula` wrapper here; `MEDIAN(IF(cond,range))` recalculates against the first cell only → "different value of the right type". | KNOWLEDGE | Narrow additive rule naming the exact formula subclass (prompt Rule 3) |
| 4 | **Coordinate/off-by-one via `df.iloc` offsets** | 48924 (fatal, whole answer shifted 1 row), 5835 (read window `iloc[2:19]` for `C3:C19`), 38985 | `read_excel(header=0)` makes `iloc[0]` == Excel row 2; a second `+1` shifts everything. Read-back reused the same arithmetic, so the bug was invisible. | STRUCTURE | "Address graded cells by literal A1, write and read back by the same address" (prompt Rule 2 + template stage 3.1) |
| 5 | **Evidence in the workbook read then discarded** | 38985, 48924, 49036, 42354, 11842 | Pre-filled worked-example rows and explicit bound cells were printed and then contradicted; 42354 overwrote 5 already-correct cells with formulas that resolved to `#N/A`. | KNOWLEDGE + STRUCTURE | Mandatory stage-1 inspection of `answer_position` (template) + "treat what's there as a spec" (prompt Rule 4) |
| 6 | **Format/scope literalism** — decimals, blanks, one-past-the-end | 49036 (`"0%"` vs required `.00` → `67%` not `66.67%`), 42354 (wrote `""` into a must-be-blank cell + 1 cell past the range) | Instruction stated the format; agent noticed the conflict in a comment and guessed. | KNOWLEDGE | Prompt Rule 5 |
| 7 | **Stated caveat asserted away instead of handled** | 11842 (94/96 — "each person has two rows" → 2 cells HIGHER), 38985 (duplicate lookup values), 51359 | Agent wrote a comment claiming its approach "will correctly" handle the warned-about trap, and never printed a number proving it. | STRUCTURE | Prompt Rule 5 bullet 2 ("show the number, don't assert") |
| 8 | **No-op re-runs / silent ambiguity resolution** | 51359 (3 write+verify rounds, byte-identical `4.0 6.0 9.0 4.0` each time, never noticed), 33722, 49036 | No recovery guidance for "my own fix changed nothing". | RECOVERY | Prompt Rule 6 + template closing line |

Also failing and covered: **53647** (in the failing traces but not in the instruction's list of
11 — formula → error text + `str` where `float`/`int` expected; covered by clusters 1/3).

## Changes made this iteration

| cluster | edit class (from system-prompt SKILL) | file | what & why it generalizes | protects passing? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| all | **#7 add role/goal line + #8 tighten output contract** — new "How you are scored" section | `prompt.md` (new file) | States what the grader actually compares: values in `answer_position`, **including python type**; blank-vs-value; error strings; and that Sheet-Level grades the whole region. This is a fact no trace shows the agent knowing, and it is the domain's fixed contract, not a task specific. | Yes — describes the grading the 29 passing tasks already satisfy |
| 2 | **#4 add a rule the source requires** + **#5 worked example** | `prompt.md` Rule 1 | Default = `load_workbook` → assign A1 cells → `save`, with a 5-line copyable idiom; explicit escape clause for "generating the entire sheet" or "re-shape (sort/insert/delete/clear-and-repopulate)"; plus the two-handle `data_only=True`-to-read / plain-to-write idiom. | Yes — see blast radius below; escape clause + two-handle rule were added specifically to protect 13-1, 297-42, 353-29, 48608, 58147 |
| 4 | **#1 rewrite positively framed** | `prompt.md` Rule 2 | "Write `ws["C2"]…ws["C13"]` and read back the same addresses" — names the target instead of prohibiting offsets, and states the `header=0` off-by-one reason. | Yes — additive; no passing trace depends on iloc-offset writing being unmentioned |
| 3 | **#4 stricter condition on an existing permission** (NOT a broadening) | `prompt.md` Rule 3 | Formulas stay allowed (grader recalculates) — literal value REQUIRED only for array/CSE aggregates and for formulas whose inputs are unverified error/blank sources. Narrowed by naming the discriminating condition. | Yes — the 5 passing formula tasks use `IF`/`SUMIFS`/`COUNTIFS`/`INDEX-MATCH`/text fns, none array-entered |
| 1 | **#2 add the reason to a bare rule** | `prompt.md` Rule 3 | "No Excel here, nothing recalculates, openpyxl stores no cached value, so the grader is the first thing to evaluate your formula" — the rationale that makes verification-by-formula-echo visibly worthless, extending to cases I didn't enumerate. | Yes |
| 5 | **#4 add omitted rule** | `prompt.md` Rule 4 | Pre-filled cells = spec; disagreement means re-examine your interpretation before overwriting; read stated bounds instead of `min()`/`max()`. Carved out: applies to VALUES not formatting, and does not apply where the instruction says delete/clear/replace. | Yes — carve-outs added after checking 13-1, 379-36, 47827, 48588 |
| 6 | **#4 + #1** | `prompt.md` Rule 5 | Decimals/percent decide the graded string; caveats are traps to handle in code and print; write only the named cells; leave blank by leaving UNWRITTEN (`""`/`0` is a value). | Yes — 56427's gold answer is mostly blank, and this rule endorses leaving blanks |
| 8 | **recovery guidance** | `prompt.md` Rule 6 | Identical output ⇒ your edit did nothing; for genuine ambiguity compute both readings and pick the one reproducing the example cells. | Yes — additive, only fires after a mismatch |
| 1, 4 | **#6 restructure into an ORDERED procedure** + **#8 tighten contract** | `task_template.md` | Replaced the flat 3-item list with 3 ordered STAGES with stage 1 (inspect `answer_position` + `data_type` by A1) as a precondition of stage 2 (compute + print + write), and a stage 3 checklist of 4 items that can FAIL. Deleted "Reply without a code block when you are satisfied the saved file is correct" in favour of "only once Stage 3 printed real values from the saved file and every item came out clean. An existing output file is not evidence of a correct one." | Yes |
| 2 | **#8 tighten contract** | `task_template.md` stage 3.4 | Sheet-Level only: diff the whole graded range output-vs-source and print every differing cell with before/after value+type; untouched cells changing type ⇒ you re-serialized, go edit in place. | Yes — conditioned on `Sheet-Level`; cannot fire on the 25 passing Cell-Level tasks |
| — | **#1 rewrite for clarity** | `task_template.md` field list | `spreadsheet_content` now labelled a pandas PREVIEW, not ground truth ("text-stored numbers, dates, blanks and merged headers all appear transformed there"). Explains why stage 1 exists. | Yes |

**Constraint-line accounting for the one deletion.** I removed the template's old round-3
sentence and its "reply without a code block when you are satisfied" ending. Both constraints
survive, strictly stronger: "re-open output_path and print the values in answer_position" is
now stage 3.1 (with the A1-addressing and `data_only` traps named), and the stop condition is
now stage-3-clean rather than agent satisfaction. No rule was dropped.

## Verify-the-fix (one line per change; trace evidence → new behavior)

- **Vacuous verification (all 11).** 33722 trace prints `Cell E2: Formula==MEDIAN(IF(($C2:$C$12<=0.01)...`, then the agent replies with nothing and stops → stage 3.1 now says a graded cell reading back as a string starting with `=` means "you have verified nothing about what the grader will see", and stage 2 requires the computed value to be PRINTED, so the agent has a number to compare against. Verified against the scorer: 33722's feedback is "5 cells hold a different value of the right type", i.e. the grader read *numbers* — confirming the formula-echo told the agent nothing about the graded value.
- **48924 off-by-one.** Trace writes `df_output.iloc[i + 1, 2] = missing_dates_list[i]` and "verifies" with `print(df_verify.iloc[1:13, 2])` — same offset, so the 1-row shift is invisible; feedback: "11 of 12 differ … 5 cells were CHANGED although the expected value is the cell's own original input". Prompt Rule 2 + stage 3.1 forbid reading back by offset and require literal `ws["C2"]…ws["C13"]`, which lands on the graded cells and would have shown C2 still holding its original date.
- **5835.** Trace verifies with `df_verify.iloc[2:19, 2]` for range `C3:C19` (wrong window) and prints `NaN` at 6-7 positions across two rounds, then stops; feedback: "7 cells are empty in your output where a value is expected". Stage 3.2 makes a `None`/`NaN` in the graded range an explicit defect to fix rather than a result to report.
- **341-40 (Sheet-Level collateral).** Trace: `df = pd.read_excel(file_path)` … `df.to_excel(output_path, index=False)`; verification checked 8 of 11917 graded cells; feedback: "955 cells differ … 700 hold the CORRECT value stored as text instead of as a number/date … 955 of 955 were CHANGED although the expected value is the cell's own original input". Rule 1's in-place idiom removes the cause; stage 3.4's before/after diff would have surfaced all 955. Cross-check: passing Sheet-Level sibling 379-36 already does exactly `load_workbook` → set cells → `save`, so the new default matches a known-good trace.
- **535-20.** `cols_to_keep = [col for col in df.columns if '/description' not in str(col)]` → `to_excel`; verification printed only "Columns containing '/description': []" and "Total columns remaining: 1177" — column selection was RIGHT; feedback: 253 cells empty where a value is expected + 4 `int where str was expected`. Same two fixes; `ws.delete_cols()` on the loaded workbook is the in-place path, and the instruction ("delete all columns…") also trips Rule 1's re-shape escape clause, so the agent may legitimately choose either — but stage 3.4 catches the type/blank damage in both.
- **33722 array formula.** `MEDIAN(IF(...))` written via `ws[f'E{row}'] = formula`, 5/5 cells wrong "of the right type" → Rule 3 names `MEDIAN(IF(...))`-shaped aggregates as the case to compute in Python. Contract check: the grader clearly recalculates (11842's 94/96 formula cells matched), so the defect is the array-entry semantics, not formula-writing itself.
- **42354.** `ws[f'D{row}'] = f'=IFNA(A{row}, IFNA(B{row}, IFNA(C{row}, "")))'` written in round 1 with zero cells inspected; feedback: "6 cells hold an Excel error text … 1 cell holds a value where the expected output has none … 5 cells were CHANGED although the expected value is the cell's own original input". Three edits bite: stage 1 forces printing `answer_position` + `data_type` first (revealing D already held `Completed`, a real datetime, `ENR`…), Rule 3's error-source check distinguishes a genuine `#N/A` (`data_type == "e"`) from the text `"#N/A"`, and Rule 5's "leave blank by leaving unwritten" removes the `""` write.
- **49036 decimals.** Trace wrote `TEXT(...,"0%")` and echoed the formula text; instruction says "integer percentage … with .00 decimal"; feedback: 1/1 cell "different value of the right type". Rule 5's worked contrast (`0.6667` → `67%` vs `66.67%`) plus stage 2's "compute and print the expected answer" forces `2/3 = 0.666…` into view, which is where the decimals question becomes unavoidable.
- **11842 (94/96).** Comment in trace: "Since each person has two rows, SUMPRODUCT will correctly count all occurrences"; feedback: "2 cells hold a number HIGHER than expected". Rule 5 bullet 2 targets exactly this move — the instruction pre-warned "each person has two rows … which should affect the calculation" — and requires printing the number rather than asserting correctness. Stage 2's compute-in-Python gives the comparison value.
- **51359 no-op loop.** Rounds 1/3/5 wrote, 2/4/6 verified, output byte-identical `4.0 6.0 9.0 4.0` every time across two different slice edits, never noticed. Rule 6 + the template's closing line make identical re-run output an explicit signal to investigate rather than re-save.
- **38985 worked example.** Trace printed Table 1's example row `AAA | Red | Black | Blue | Yellow` and then adopted a contradictory nth-occurrence rule, getting exactly the 2 cells the example would have fixed; it also wrote `df.iloc[6, 3] = 'Red'` with the comment "just in case, though not in answer_position". Rule 4 (example row is the spec; disagreement means re-examine your interpretation) + Rule 5 ("do not fill nearby cells just in case").

## Blast radius per edit (BOUNDED unless stated) — and the three rules I RESCOPED because a passing trace said they were unsafe

I used a read-only subagent to audit 15 passing traces against draft rules. It flagged three
real hazards; all three are fixed in the shipped text, and this is the part of the iteration
I'd most want a future run to preserve:

1. **"Untouched cells must equal the original" would have BROKEN 13-1.** 13-1's instruction
   literally says "delete the old ranges in the 'LISTS' sheet before populating", and the
   winning turn is `new_lists.iloc[2:32, 0:4] = ""` clearing stale rows INSIDE the graded
   range `A3:D32`. Also 379-36's gold overwrites 2 pre-filled cells. → The preserve-original
   language is scoped to stage 3.4's *diff and review* ("the only differences should be the
   ones the instruction asked for" — a diff to inspect, not an equality to enforce), and
   Rule 4 carries an explicit carve-out: "when the instruction tells you to delete, clear, or
   replace existing content, do it".
2. **"No `None`/`NaN` in `answer_position`" would have BROKEN 56427.** Its gold answer leaves
   most of `H2:S28` (324 cells) blank and the instruction says "preserve blanks as blanks (not
   zeros)". → Stage 3.2 and Rule 5 both carry "unless the instruction says those cells are
   legitimately blank, in which case blank is correct". Also I did NOT write a type-homogeneity
   rule: 46646's gold is deliberately mixed (`0` as int, others float) per its formatting rule.
3. **Bare "use openpyxl instead of pandas" would have BROKEN 48608 and 58147.** Both read a
   source column that is formula-generated (48608's instruction says the column comes from a
   "unique, filter formula"); a naive `load_workbook(path)` returns `"=UNIQUE(FILTER(...))"`,
   `float()` raises, and results silently become "Not Found". → Rule 1 ships with the
   two-handle idiom (`data_only=True` to read, plain handle to write) and the tell "if a value
   you read back looks like a string starting with `=`, you used the wrong handle".

Remaining blast radius, by class:
- **`to_excel` users among passing tasks (11): 13-1, 297-42, 353-29, 32902, 41265, 48588, 48608, 48921, 56920, 58147, 44913.** Rule 1's escape clause covers 13-1 (clear+repopulate), 297-42 (target sheet starts empty — "0 data row(s)"), 353-29 (graded range A1:B90 *is* the whole sheet). The other 7 are few-cell edits of populated sheets that Rule 1 moves to openpyxl; I checked each writes plain scalars to `answer_position` only, so the openpyxl path produces the same graded values — and 44913 is positive evidence, having failed twice with `to_excel` (`[nan, 117.17, nan, …]`) and passed only after switching to openpyxl with its own comment "to avoid pandas' NaN conversion". Rule 1 is the one edit I'd class as **borderline-unbounded** (it changes method on ~7 passing tasks even though it should not change their graded values); the escape clause and two-handle rule are what bound it.
- **Turn budget.** Stages add turns, so I checked the two passing tasks that hit the 30-turn cap: 56920 saved a correct file at turn **1** and 56427 at turn **5**; turns 6-30 in both are byte-identical no-op re-saves. Extra verification turns cannot starve their save. (Rule 6 should in fact end those degenerate loops early.)
- **Rule 4 vs. formatting.** 47827's instruction says "bold and fill all boxed values" over an already-populated column G; "don't overwrite a cell that already holds the answer" could have skipped the `cell.font`/`cell.fill` assignment too. → Rule 4 states it is about values, and "apply that formatting to every cell the instruction names, including cells whose value you left alone".
- **48588** is fully pre-filled with its own gold (`1.0, 2.0, …`); Rule 4 could make the agent copy the input through. That still matches the gold (the passing run rewrote `1.0`→`1` and also passed, so the grader tolerates both).

## Process & features used
- **Subagents:** yes — 2 parallel read-only diagnosis subagents (failing traces split into two
  groups of 5-6) and 1 read-only blast-radius auditor over 15 passing traces. No worktrees:
  the edit is 2 files and merging was unnecessary; all edits merged by hand into this one
  candidate. I also ran direct census scripts over all 40 traces (method used, turns, formula
  vs literal, feedback-phrase frequency, `data_only`/`soffice` grep).
- **Prior iterations read:** none exist — `RUNMAP.md` and `LEDGER.md` are empty, no
  `prior_iterations/`, no `rejected.jsonl`/`history.jsonl`. Nothing to build on or avoid.
- **Validated** the placeholder contract mechanically: all 6 required placeholders present,
  `max_turns` present, no unknown braces, and `body.format(**vals)` renders with every
  required value appearing in the output.

## Good things to PRESERVE (do not let a future iteration undo these)
- **The grader RECALCULATES formulas** (42198, 52807, 41589, 39515, 49801 all pass with
  formula-only outputs; 11842 got 94/96 formula cells right). Never add a blanket "write
  values, not formulas" rule — it regresses 5+ passing tasks.
- **Cell-Level grading only checks `answer_position`**, so don't argue Rule 1 from collateral
  damage on Cell-Level tasks; the Sheet-Level diff is where preservation actually pays.
- **The three carve-outs above** (delete/clear instructions; legitimately-blank cells;
  `data_only=True` for reading formula-backed sources). Each was added because a specific
  passing trace would otherwise break: 13-1, 56427, 48608/58147.
- The pandas `spreadsheet_content` preview is NOT ground truth about cell types.

## Deliberately skipped (cluster + why)
- **Nothing was skipped for lack of effort.** All 11 listed failures plus 53647 are covered.
- **No per-task semantic fix** for 51359 (whether "total of consecutive 1's" means summing
  streak lengths or counting qualifying groups) or 38985 (which duplicate-pairing rule). Those
  need the gold answer, and encoding either reading would be a task-specific literal that
  overfits. Instead both are attacked generically: Rule 6 requires computing BOTH readings and
  picking the one that reproduces the pre-filled example cells (38985's example row and
  51359's data extent are present in their workbooks).
- **No formula-evaluation tooling** suggested (LibreOffice headless / `formulas` / `pycel`).
  It would be the highest-leverage change to cluster 1, but the sandbox shows no evidence of
  those being available and this capability is prose-only — a prompt telling the agent to
  shell out to `soffice` would be a speculative edit. Recorded in FRAMEWORK_IMPROVEMENTS.md.
